facts.fact: The Minister of Labour and Home Affairs requested a 2026/27 recurrent provision of P108,505,050 for the Department of Civil and National Registration to cover, among others, Omang production and the maintenance of the Births and Deaths Registration System and the National Identification System (para 43); no share for the BDRS is given.

The minister's speech places the Births and Deaths Registration System under department 0411, Civil and National Registration, of the Ministry of Labour and Home Affairs, which he says manages citizens' life events from birth to death.

The minister reported that the digitisation of ministry functions including online registration of births and deaths, marriages and change of surname is completed and will go live once the 1-Gov platform takes off; it was not live at the date of the speech (para 18).

note: The class of the online registration service is uncertain: the speech names it as registration of births and deaths online without saying who makes the record, so it may be a public portal. Also stated, with no system named: the Births and Deaths Registration Act 2025 was assented to in August 2025 and comes into effect in 2026 once its Regulations are done (para 11). The BDRS itself is named but not described.
